task_instance: Fulfill a representative general NVIDIA App request -- "Show my NVIDIA driver status" -- by connecting to the local NVIDIA App MCP server, discovering tools, and calling the read-only nvapp_client_get_driver_status tool to report systemType, installed driver version/channel, preferred channel, and recommended drivers.
blocker_detail: The skill operates NVIDIA App exclusively through its local MCP server, which the skill's own Prerequisites require to run inside a Windows host with NVIDIA App (version 11.0.9.5xx+) installed and its NvContainer-hosted MCP plugin running on an NVIDIA GPU system. This runtime is Linux x86_64 (uname: Linux vm 6.18.44-fc-v185) with no Windows layer, no NVIDIA GPU (no nvidia-smi, no display/3D controller in device listing), and no NVIDIA App or NvAppMcpServer executable anywhere on the filesystem. The stdio bridge path is a Windows %ProgramFiles% .exe and the documented default loopback HTTP endpoint is a placeholder the run rules forbid reaching. No nvapp_ tools are advertised in this session's catalog and none can be registered because the backing proprietary NVIDIA App MCP service does not exist and is not installable on this platform. Every supported deliverable (driver status, game optimization, laptop features, and all nvapp_overlay_ recording/screenshot/stats/filter operations) depends on this unavailable server, so no concrete task instance could be attempted. Per run rules I did not write any stub/mock of the NVIDIA MCP server.
evidence: cd into work dir. `uname -a` -> Linux vm 6.18.44-fc-v185 x86_64 (not Windows). `find / -iname 'NVIDIA App.exe'` and `find / -iname 'NvAppMcpServer.exe'` -> no matches. `command -v nvidia-smi` -> not found; no NVIDIA driver present. `lspci | grep -i -E 'vga|nvidia|3d'` -> no display/3D controller listed (no GPU). Loopback TCP listeners present are only the agent's own proxy/tooling ports (e.g. 0100007F entries), none is an NVIDIA App MCP server; the skill's documented HTTP endpoint is a redacted placeholder that run rules forbid contacting. Conclusion: the required local NVIDIA App MCP server (Windows + NVIDIA GPU, proprietary) is absent and not installable in this runtime, so the core deliverable cannot be produced or verified. No result files beyond this one were produced.
